reasons.A: Measured, courteous period register and a mix of short declaratives with longer sentences, but the past tense and the closing explanation of the joke are less the author's dry, present-tense essayist manner.
reasons.B: Keeps the author's present-tense generalising about the type, urbane irony and understated punchlines ('an unusually attentive audience'), and lets the joke land without spelling it out, as the passage does.
reasons.C: Modern, choppy rhythm with punchy fragments and a summarising coda; it explains every joke and reads as a contemporary explainer, not the author's genteel, wry understatement.
